newsitem.title: USA: US Gulf gasoline steepens trajectory in late trade.
newsitem.headline: US Gulf gasoline steepens trajectory in late trade.

text.p: U.S. Gulf Coast conventional unleaded gasoline stole the limelight on an otherwise sleepy trading day Tuesday, players said, jumping another two cents a gallon on the heels of similar gains Monday.

Gulf traders described continued tightness of "M4" unleaded and slim activity as many players remained away at the American Petroleum Institute's (API) annual meeting being held this week in Washington, D.C.

Prompt front-33rd-cycle "M4" was talked between 1.75 cents and 2.25 cents over December futures, one cent firmer than Monday differentials, players said, with one deal mentioned but not confirmed at 2.50 cents over.
Gulf traders kept a sharp lookout Tuesday for the reappearance of the Wall Street brokerage firm Morgan Stanley, which they said snapped up as many as 300,000 barrels of "M4" Monday.
"I didn't see them today, but I think Morgan Stanley bought 300,000 to 400,000 barrels yesterday," one player said.
"They probably owe refiners, were expecting the market to go down, and now have to short cover," he said, adding that razor-thin activity Tuesday allowed prices to rise on limited numbers of deals.
